facts.statement: Invictarx is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur that lived in New Mexico during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the lower Campanian stage around 78.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Invictarx (meaning "unconquerable fortress") is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from New Mexico that lived during the Late Cretaceous (lower Campanian, 78.5 Ma)

facts.statement: The only known species, Invictarx zephyri, is represented by three isolated and incomplete postcranial skeletons.
facts.quote: The type and only species, Invictarx zephyri, is known from three isolated, incomplete postcranial skeletons.

facts.statement: The genus was named and described in 2018 by paleontologists Andrew T. McDonald and Douglas G. Wolfe.
facts.quote: It was named in 2018 by Andrew T. McDonald and Douglas G. Wolfe.

facts.statement: The first fossil specimen was discovered in May 2011 by Daniel Williamson in the upper Allison Member of the Menefee Formation in the San Juan Basin.
facts.quote: In May 2011, an incomplete postcranial skeleton of an ankylosaur was discovered from the upper Allison Member of the Menefee Formation, San Juan Basin by Daniel Williamson.

facts.statement: Two additional specimens were found in October 2011 by Andrew T. McDonald and in October 2015 by Keith Brockmann.
facts.quote: A second incomplete postcranial skeleton was discovered in October 2011 by Andrew T. McDonald while a third specimen was discovered in October 2015 by Keith Brockmann.

facts.statement: The name Invictarx combines the Latin words for 'invincible' and 'fortress' to reflect the animal's heavy armor.
facts.quote: The generic name, Invictarx, is derived from the Latin words "invictus" (invincible or unconquerable) and "arx" (fortress), in reference to the fact that Invictarx, like all other ankylosaurs, were well-armoured.

facts.statement: The species name zephyri refers to the western wind and the blustery conditions at the fossil discovery sites.
facts.quote: The specific name, zephyri, is derived from is the genitive form of the Greek noun Zephyrus, meaning (of the) western wind, referring to the "blustery conditions that prevail among the outcrops where the specimens were discovered".

facts.statement: Invictarx shares similarities with the dinosaur Glyptodontopelta, which is found in the Ojo Alamo Formation of New Mexico.
facts.quote: Invictarx shares similarities with Glyptodontopelta from the Naashoibito member of the Ojo Alamo Formation, New Mexico.

facts.statement: Invictarx is distinguished by osteoderms with a smooth surface texture, abundant random pits, and few or no neurovascular grooves.
facts.quote: McDonald & Wolfe (2018) diagnosed Invictarx based on the cervical or pectoral, thoracic, and pelvic osteoderms exhibiting an overall smooth surface texture, with little to no projecting rugosity, with abundant pits distributed randomly over the entire external surface, and with no neurovascular grooves or a small number of bifurcating and non-bifurcating neurovascular grooves distributed randomly

facts.statement: The animal likely possessed a co-ossified pelvic shield made of uniformly sized polygonal osteoderms, similar to Nodosaurus and Stegopelta.
facts.quote: and the presence of possible a co-ossified pelvic shield that consists of polygonal osteoderms of uniform size, similar to Nodosaurus, Stegopelta, Glyptodontopelta, Europelta and Aletopelta.

facts.statement: The preserved vertebrae are identified as middle dorsal vertebrae based on comparisons with Sauropelta and Europelta, but they lack fused ribs.
facts.quote: Based on Sauropelta and Europelta, the vertebrae are identified as middle dorsal vertebrae, although there are no indications of ribs fused to the three dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The neural canal in the vertebrae is ellipse-shaped with its axis oriented toward the upper edge and sides.
facts.quote: The neural canal is ellipse-shaped with its axis oriented towards the upper edge and sides.

facts.statement: The ulnar condyle of the forearm was larger than the radial condyle.
facts.quote: The ulnar condyle was larger than the radial condyle.

facts.statement: Invictarx is classified as a monospecific genus within the nodosaurid dinosaur family.
facts.quote: Invictarx (meaning "unconquerable fortress") is a monospecific genus of nodosaurid dinosaur

facts.statement: Some of Invictarx's cervical or pectoral osteoderms were up to 1.8 cm thick at their base and thinned to 0.6 cm at the edges.
facts.quote: The osteoderm is 1.8 cm thick and gradually thins towards the margins where it attains a thickness of 0.6 cm.

facts.statement: The keel on certain Invictarx osteoderms measured 2.2 cm thick before thinning down to just 0.6 cm.
facts.quote: The keel of the osteoderm has a thickness of 2.2 cm and thins to only 0.6 cm.

facts.statement: The most complete thoracic osteoderm found in the holotype specimen was only 5.1 cm wide.
facts.quote: The most complete thoracic osteoderm is small compared to the other osteoderms referred to the holotype and is only 5.1 cm wide.

facts.statement: One of Invictarx's cervical osteoderms features a keel that is strongly offset to the side, similar to the genus Edmontonia.
facts.quote: The osteoderm has a keel that is strongly laterally offset, as in Edmontonia.

facts.statement: Invictarx lived during the lower Campanian stage, approximately 78.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Invictarx is known from the upper Allison Member of the Menefee Formation which has been dated to the lower Campanian stage, 78.5 Ma.

facts.statement: Invictarx inhabited a widespread alluvial floodplain environment characterized by mudstone, siltstone, sandstone, and coal.
facts.quote: The Menefee Formation represents a widespread alluvial floodplain and consists of mudstone, siltstone, sandstone, and coal.

facts.quote: genus_authority: McDonald & Wolfe, 2018

facts.statement: Invictarx lived alongside various dinosaurs including the tyrannosaurid Dynamoterror, the ceratopsid Menefeeceratops, the hadrosaurid Ornatops, and a dromaeosaurid similar to Saurornitholestes.
facts.quote: Invictarx was contemporaneous with an indeterminate ankylosaur, the tyrannosaurid theropod Dynamoterror, an indeterminate hadrosaurid, the centrosaurine ceratopsid Menefeeceratops, the brachylophosaurin hadrosaurid Ornatops, an indeterminate tyrannosaurid, and a dromaeosaurid similar to Saurornitholestes.

facts.statement: Contemporary non-dinosaur animals included the alligatoroids Brachychampsa and Deinosuchus, as well as various indeterminate turtles.
facts.quote: Non-dinosaur taxa contemporaneous with Invictarx include an indeterminate crocodylian, the alligatoroids Brachychampsa and Deinosuchus, an indeterminate baenid turtle, an indeterminate turtle, and an indeterminate trionychid turtle.
